events.title: Which cities will Waymo launch in by December 31?
events.description:

events.title: Will Tesla release Optimus by...?
events.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla releases a humanoid, bipedal robot (such as Optimus) by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying product is a humanoid, bipedal robot intended for consumer use and newly introduced. Non-humanoid robotics, accessories, internal factory deployments, employee-only programs, and partner/enterprise pilots do not qualify.

To be considered “released,” the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the timeframe via an official Tesla consumer channel (e.g., tesla.com) with a live checkout or paid preorder/deposit. Announcements, unveilings, demos, or waitlists with “register interest” pages without payment do not suffice. Availability in any region counts if it is open to the general public.

The primary resolution source will be official statements and materials from Tesla.

events.title: Two SpaceX Starships dock together by…?
events.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if two SpaceX Starships successfully execute a docking maneuver in a stable Earth orbit between market creation and the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying docking maneuver must physically join two vessels, matching in velocity, into a connected structure via mating hardware for at least 60 continuous seconds. The two vessels must be in stable Earth orbit with a perigee of at least 100 kilometers above the Earth’s surface.

events.title: SpaceX becomes a US mobile carrier by ___?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if SpaceX makes a mobile phone plan available for purchase in the United States between market creation and 11:59 PM ET on the specified date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Plans offered by a carrier that SpaceX acquires a controlling interest in will count once the acquisition is completed and the plan satisfies all other requirements of these rules. Availability to customers in at least one U.S. state will qualify. Availability limited to customers outside the United States, internal or employee testing, waitlists, and invite-only programs will not qualify.

Announcements, pre-orders, and deposits alone will not qualify; the mobile phone plan must be available by the deadline. Acquiring spectrum licenses or network assets, or obtaining regulatory approval, alone will not qualify.

events.title: Will Apple release a new product line before 2028?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Apple launches a new product line between market creation and December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "new product line" is an Apple-branded hardware product that establishes a distinct product category based on its functionality and intended use. A new name alone is insufficient, and reuse of a previous product name does not disqualify an otherwise qualifying product.

New models, sizes, generations, editions, or renamed versions of an existing product family will not qualify solely because they introduce a new design, form factor, feature, or name. However, a product may qualify if its functionality and intended use establish a distinct product category, even if it shares features, technology, or branding with an existing Apple product. Products Apple has sold before market creation, including HomeView, and subsequent updates to those products will not qualify unless those updates independently meet the criteria for a new product line.

For example, the original Apple Vision Pro and HomeView launches constituted new product lines; iPhone Air and AirPods Pro 3 did not.

Software, services, accessories (e.g., cases, chargers, keyboards, or Apple Pencil), and Beats-branded products will not qualify. An accessory is hardware whose primary purpose is to support, control, or extend the functionality of another product, rather than perform a distinct primary function of its own. Compatibility with, or a setup requirement involving, another device does not alone make a product an accessory.

A product is considered launched when it becomes officially available to public customers, through delivery or physical purchase.

The primary resolution source will be official information from Apple, including Apple Newsroom and the Apple Store; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
